title: Is Lobby Marble & Terrazzo Honing and Sealing Included in Standard Cleaning or Billed Extra?
seoTitle: Extra Charge for Marble & Terrazzo Honing? Included vs Add-On Quotes
metaDescription: Extra charge marble terrazzo honing audit: what base retainers include vs $2-$6.50/sq ft work orders. Check your janitorial bids in our Quote Comparator.
excerpt: Most janitorial base retainers cover daily stone care but not diamond honing or sealing, which is billed as a separate project work order. This audit guide shows exactly where vendors draw the line and how to keep surprise invoices out of your lobby budget.
quickAnswer: Standard janitorial retainers almost always include daily dust mopping and neutral damp mopping of marble and terrazzo, but honing, polishing, and sealing are billed extra as project work orders at roughly $1.75-$6.50 per sq ft. Some Class A contracts fold a quarterly maintenance polish into the monthly fee, usually adding $0.03-$0.08 per sq ft of stone per month, so read the periodic-services schedule before assuming coverage.

blocks.text: Janitorial contracts separate routine services, which are priced into the monthly retainer, from periodic or project services, which are either scheduled at a set frequency inside the fee or invoiced separately. Stone honing sits squarely on the project side for most vendors because it requires diamond tooling, planetary machines, slurry handling, and technicians with stone training that a standard night crew does not have. The confusion arises because proposals often say marble floor care, which can mean anything from a damp mop to a full restoration.

blocks.caption: How stone floor tasks are typically treated in US janitorial contracts
rows: Nightly dust mop and neutral damp mop
Spot spill removal and walk-off mat vacuuming
Included weekly or nightly in larger lobbies
Maintenance polish with stone pads or powder
Sometimes included quarterly in Class A contracts
Terrazzo coating strip and restoration grind

items: Hard floor maintenance as needed: this phrase lets the vendor decide when polishing happens and bill each visit as extra.
Stone care per manufacturer recommendations: ties scope to a document you may not have and rarely defines frequency.
Periodic services quoted upon request: means nothing periodic is in the base price.
Specialty surfaces excluded: common catch-all that removes marble, terrazzo, granite, and wood from routine scope.
Damage resulting from pre-existing conditions: acceptable, but require a documented pre-start walkthrough with photos so etching caused by the vendor's chemicals is not blamed on the building.

blocks.title: The etch trap
blocks.text: If your janitorial vendor uses acidic restroom bowl cleaner or citrus degreaser near the lobby and etches the marble, they may then quote the repair as an add-on honing work order. Require neutral pH chemistry for stone in the scope, list approved products, and state that damage caused by unapproved chemicals is repaired at vendor expense.
Bundled vs Work-Order Pricing: A Side-by-Side

Take a 20,000 sq ft office with a 2,500 sq ft marble lobby. Nightly janitorial at five nights per week falls in the 10,000-24,999 sq ft bracket at $0.07-$0.12 per sq ft per visit, or about $30,310-$51,960 per month at 21.65 visits. Below are two ways the stone program could be priced.

Polish, seal, and hone ordered when needed

blocks.text: The hybrid structure tends to work best for multi-tenant office buildings. Routine maintenance polishing goes into the monthly fee, and the contract includes a rate card for seal refresh and full honing so the property manager can issue a work order without rebidding each time.
Tools and Supplies That Signal a Serious Stone Program

When walking a vendor's night shift, look at what is on the cart. Color-coded split microfiber like the Rubbermaid HYGEN 16x16 cloths, rated for about 500 commercial launderings, lets crews keep a dedicated stone-only color so restroom chemistry never touches the lobby. A locking cabinet cart such as the Suncast Commercial housekeeping model keeps acidic products contained during day porter shifts. Even lobby receptacles matter: a heavy steel unit like the Safco Public Square 37-gallon receptacle should sit on felt glides so liner changes do not scratch the polish.
How to Audit Your Current Contract

items.name: Pull the scope and periodic schedule
items.text: Find every mention of marble, terrazzo, stone, or hard floor and note frequency and whether it is in the base price.

items.name: Review 12 months of invoices
items.text: Total every work order tied to the lobby floor to see your true annual stone spend.

items.name: Request a rate card
items.text: Ask the vendor to quote per-sq-ft rates for maintenance polish, seal refresh, and full hone to attach as a contract exhibit.

items.name: Define chemistry and damage terms
items.text: Add approved neutral cleaners and a vendor-pays clause for chemical damage.

items.name: Benchmark against a stone specialist
items.text: Get one direct bid from a restoration contractor; janitorial vendors often subcontract and add 10-25%.

faqs.q: Should honing be in the base janitorial price?
faqs.a: Generally no. Full diamond honing is a periodic restoration that happens every 12-60 months, so building it into a monthly fee means prepaying for work on the vendor's timeline. It is cleaner to bundle maintenance polishing and keep honing on a pre-priced work-order rate card.

faqs.q: What markup do janitorial vendors add when subcontracting stone work?
faqs.a: Typical markups run 10-25% for coordination, insurance, and supervision. That can be fair if the janitorial vendor manages scheduling and quality, but you should know the subcontractor's identity and confirm they carry their own certificate of insurance naming the owner and property manager.

faqs.q: Who is responsible if a polished floor causes a slip?
faqs.a: Responsibility depends on contract indemnification language and the work performed. Require the stone vendor to follow wet-floor signage practices, document cure times, and use products with acceptable slip resistance. Have both vendors carry general liability with the owner as additional insured.

faqs.q: Are sealers and polishing compounds covered by HazCom requirements?
faqs.a: Yes. Under OSHA's Hazard Communication standard, vendors must maintain Safety Data Sheets and label secondary containers. Ask that SDS binders for stone products be kept in the janitorial closet alongside daily chemicals, and that low-VOC options be used where the building follows Green Seal or LEED operations policies.

faqs.q: How do I convert a bundled quarterly polish to a monthly fee?
faqs.a: Multiply the per-visit polish price by four visits, add any annual seal, and divide by 12. For a 2,500 sq ft lobby at $0.80 per sq ft per polish, four visits equal $8,000 a year, or about $667 per month. Compare that monthly accrual against your historical work-order spend.
